subject: Animation
title: Pixar and Streaming: The Pandemic Shift
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pixar and Streaming: The Pandemic Shift usable.

hook.text: During the pandemic, Disney sent three Pixar films straight to Disney+ instead of theaters.

buildup.text: Soul, Luca, and Turning Red skipped the big screen entirely. Pixar staff felt their work was devalued.

discovery.text: The films attracted huge streaming audiences but earned no box office revenue for comparison.

twist.text: Disney sent live-action films to theaters during the same period, making Pixar staff feel like second-class.

climax.text: The streaming pivot raised questions about whether Pixar films would ever feel like events again.

punchline.text: Pixar made movies for the big screen and got a small one.

quiz.question: How did the pandemic streaming pivot affect Pixar?
options: It had no impact on the studio
Three films went straight to Disney+, demoralizing staff who felt their work was devalued
It led to Pixar leaving Disney

details.summary: Disney sent several Pixar films directly to Disney+ during the pandemic, bypassing theatrical release. Soul, Luca, and Turning Red debuted on streaming, raising concerns that Pixar's films were being treated as fodder for Disney's streaming ambitions rather than theatrical events.
details.whyItMatters: Sending Pixar films to streaming devalued them in audiences' eyes. If animated features are free streaming content rather than theatrical events, the perceived worth of animation as an art form diminishes alongside its box office revenue.
takeaways: Soul, Luca, and Turning Red were sent directly to Disney+ without theatrical release
The streaming-first approach raised concerns about devaluing Pixar's brand
Pixar staff publicly expressed frustration about their films skipping theaters

faq.question: Why did Disney send Pixar films to streaming instead of theaters?
faq.answer: Pandemic theater closures provided the initial reason, but Disney continued the practice after theaters reopened. Pixar films drove Disney+ subscriptions effectively. Critics argued Disney sacrificed Pixar's theatrical brand to serve streaming growth metrics.

faq.question: How did the streaming releases affect Pixar internally?
faq.answer: Pixar artists and leadership expressed frustration that years of work premiered as home-viewing content. The artistic and cultural impact of theatrical premieres — the communal experience, the marketing events — was lost. Inside Out 2's theatrical release was partly a response to these concerns.
